content.thinking:
I'm sizing up the phoenix design, giving it a roughly 1.2m body, 3.5m wingspan, and a 2m streaming tail, and deciding it should stand perched on its talons with wings spread in a display-like pose rather than flying.

I'm settling on a Genshin-style cel-shaded look: pyro palette of crimson, scarlet, orange, gold, and cream, with gold filigree trim and petal-like feather shapes. Now I'm working out the skeleton coordinates, placing the hips around y=0.7 and body center near (0, 0.95, 0) with the chest leaning forward.

Working out wing and feather geometry...

I'll orthogonalize those axes myself for the extrude call, then paint a gradient along the feather length—crimson at the base fading through orange to gold at the tip—layering in cel shading so top faces read lit and undersides read shadowed.

Nested paints inherit the outer `s` coordinate, so the gradient logic should propagate correctly. For texel density, I'm estimating total painted area across ~80 feathers plus the body comes to roughly 10m², which at a 2048 paint sheet gives fine resolution—around 4mm per texel—so I'll stick with 2048 rather than bumping to 4096, keeping that hand-painted feel. I'm also considering flat palette colors as a simpler alternative to full gradients for some feathers.

Actually gradient-painted feathers with rachis lines and slanted barb stripes look much better, so I'm designing a cel paint pattern that darkens along the central spine and adds subtle barb striping, while keeping the texel size around 2-4mm to resolve the ~12mm barb spacing. For the flight feather silhouette itself, I'm shaping a slightly asymmetric leaf-like outline with a pointed tip.

Writing feather outline function...

For the tail feathers I'm thinking flame-like curved ribbons swept along a curve with a flat radius profile, painted with a crimson-to-yellow gradient along the length, plus small glowing flame-shaped card cutouts at the wing tips, tail ends, and crest to give an emissive fiery accent.

For adornments, I'll avoid literal logos and instead design a glowing gem sunburst jewel set in gold on the chest, plus gold filigree details — anklets, a tasseled crown/headpiece, a gem-set neck collar, filigree wing bracers, and gold talon caps — to get that elegant, ornate look. I'm now sketching the skeleton's spine curve from the tail root through the hips toward the neck to anchor all these pieces.

Working out the body posture, I'm angling the torso upward about 35-40° from pelvis to chest, then letting the neck arc in an S-curve up to a head position with the beak pointing forward-down, giving an overall standing height around 2.1 meters at the crest. I'm also planning spread wings with dihedral lift and a trailing tail that droops near the floor before curling upward like flames, making sure only the talons actually touch the ground plane while the tail stays just above it to avoid clipping.

Now I'm plotting the digitigrade leg structure — hip, knee, hock, and foot joints positioned to mimic real bird anatomy where the ankle bends backward and the tarsometatarsus angles down toward the toes. Each foot gets three forward toes and one back toe, each made of two or three joints with dark talon tips, totaling sixteen toe joints across both legs.

For the wings, I'm chaining shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints per side, then figuring out feather attachment — primaries rigidly fixed to the hand joint and secondaries to the forearm, balancing individual feather joints against the overall 160-joint budget by giving primaries their own joints while grouping secondaries into clusters of two or three per joint.

For the long tail streamers I'll use a two-joint chain with ribbon sweep so they flow like flames, while shorter tail feathers get single joints. Now I'm settling on a flat color palette for small parts and gradient paints for larger surfaces, mapping out crimson, scarlet, orange, and amber tones before diving into the actual code.

I'm debating adding a cool contrasting accent like teal to pop against the fire palette, but decide to stay cohesive with a Pyro-only ruby-white-gold scheme instead, maybe adding a golden iris and burgundy shadow tones. Now I'm planning the body as a loft swept along a spine chain running from pelvis to neck base, with an elliptical radius profile varying along the path.

I'm sketching out the skeleton structure: a hip joint at the root, then a spine chain running pelvis-belly-chest-neckbase, considering whether to overlap the hip and first spine joint or keep them distinct, then setting up a continuous body sweep from pelvis through the neck using bone weighting across the spine and neck chains with varying elliptical radii—thicker at the chest, tapering elsewhere.

Defining radii per-segment...

For colors, I'm thinking crimson for the back and orange-gold for the chest, with golden-cream belly feathers to give it that phoenix feel.

Blending color scales for the gradient...

Still writing fur edge logic...

I'm thinking about adding scattered flame-feather card details across the chest and neck for a shaggy plumage texture, using gradient SVG cards that carry their own color so the look stays flat without needing cel-shading.

I'm working out the flame feather shape as a leaf-like SVG with a crimson-to-orange-to-yellow gradient, a lighter central vein, and barb lines, plus a separate glowing core texture for flame wisps. To keep a hard cel look, I want to band the gradient into stepped crimson/orange/yellow sections with jagged edges using a clipPath, then I move on to designing elegant upward-sweeping wing silhouettes.

Now I'm plotting the joint positions for the left wing — shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand tip — fanning the primaries outward and upward in a V-shape like a rising phoenix, aiming for a total wingspan around 4.8 meters with primaries reaching about x=2.4, and settling on a body length of roughly 0.95 to keep the proportions believable for a mythical bird.

Now I'm working out feather geometry: defining primary, secondary, and tertial lengths, then figuring out each feather's root point along the arm (secondaries along the forearm, primaries along the wrist-to-hand segment) and its outward/backward angle, tilting progressively more outward and upward toward the wingtip to create that flaring, upswept phoenix silhouette.

Rather than extruding straight feathers, I'm considering sweeping a curved bezier path with a tapering elliptical cross-section to get a flame-like curve, then figuring out how to paint the rachis line and barb gradient onto a flat ribbon shape where the width axis doesn't map cleanly to the painting coordinates.

Alternatively, a membrane built between two curved edge paths might work better, letting me parameterize across/along the surface directly for painting the rachis down the center and barb gradients outward, with straight extruded feathers fanned and tilted as a simpler fallback stylization.

Writing the paint function logic...

Checking that the membrane edge ordering gives consistent outward normals on the closed double-sided mesh, then sketching out a feather-building function that takes a root point, direction, lift vector, length, width, and bend amount, constructing the spine curve and surrounding edges.

Still shaping the leaf profile curve...

I'm adding small glowing flame cards at the wing-feather tips for a fiery, Genshin-style elemental edge, keeping them cheap by reusing one texture per tint. For the tail, I'm planning five long ribbon streamers with gradient coloring and S-curves plus eight shorter membrane feathers to fill it out.

The streamers will end in flame glows and trail down toward floor level before curling upward at the tips, making sure the path stays above ground. For the crest, I'm sketching three swept-back flame plume streamers in gold and amber with glowing tips, plus a gold circlet with a gem for a tiara-like touch, and considering a curved falconiform beak in gold-amber tones for the head.

For the eyes, I'm debating iris color choices against the crimson-orange head -- weighing a golden-yellow iris versus a cooler turquoise for stronger contrast, and leaning toward skipping blush and brows since the flame motif should dominate.

To make the eyes pop better, I'll give the face a cream-gold mask region separate from the crimson crown, using position-based fur edge painting. Now I'm working out the head's scale and decal placement on the skull sphere, then positioning the head joint at the top of the neck with a forward-down aim direction for the bone.

For the neck, I'm plotting an S-curve of joint points rising from the base and leaning forward at the top, giving it a raptor-like posture rather than a swan curve. I'm also planning a ring of flame feather cards as a ruff at the neck base, plus a gold collar loop with a pendant gem and hanging tassels, and now I'm sketching a glowing orange gem for the chest.

Now I'm placing an octahedron gem on the chest, picking a bright gold-yellow color, and surrounding it with a gold bezel ring, six petal-shaped spikes, and two sideways gold wing extrudes for ornamentation. I'm also planning the legs with scaly gold-toned tarsus segments and feathered thighs.

Switching to crimson ruff feathers and leg feather cards, then adding gold anklet band loops with small gems, and settling on cream-gold talons for the toes. I need to make sure the toes touch the ground plane with proper geometry for the tubes and curved talon tips, keeping everything within a small height tolerance above zero. I'm also checking that overall height stays reasonable, with the crest tip around 2.2 meters and wing tips possibly extending higher.

For the wings, I'm planning a tapered bone-chain arm covered by rows of smaller covert feathers alongside the primaries, secondaries, and tertials, estimating total part counts per wing to stay under budget across both wings, tail, and crest. To save on part count I'm considering using textured feather cards for coverts and body ruffs instead of individual membrane meshes, reserving full membrane geometry for the flight feathers only.

I'm working out the orientation logic so covert cards lie flat and sweep outward from the arm, using frame normals to control lighting and flow direction, and making them double-sided with mirrored UVs so symmetry isn't an issue. Writing the feather generation math...

Writing feather paint function...

Still writing feather pattern logic...

So in shadow, the lit paint also gets darkened via shadowOf, meaning barb lines get double-darkened there, which seems fine. Now I'm considering a thin edge outline using a deep-red ink color when edge values or alpha get close to their max.

I'm settling on using edge>0.92 as the threshold for mixing in the shade color, keeping the effect subtle for now and saving flame glow for later. Then I estimate total painted surface area across feathers, body, head and tail to work out texel density at 2048 resolution, landing around 464 texels per meter with 2mm texel size, which seems adequate.

Now I'm setting up the wing skeleton chain with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints per side, parented to the chest spine joint and tagged with a wing role for skinning. Each feather gets its own joint attached to the wrist, with explicit bone assignment for the membrane geometry, and I'm laying out the primary feather roots by interpolating positions along the hand from wrist to fingertip.

I'm computing primary feather angles and lengths: inner primaries sweep around 35° back-and-out with shorter length near 0.95, while outer primaries fan to 85° with longer lengths around 1.1-1.35 and more upward lift curvature, plus a slight upward base tilt. Now I'm placing the secondary feather roots along the forearm between elbow and wrist.

Checking the overall wing span against body size, I realize the current arm proportions push the span to about 5.6x the body length, which feels too large even for a majestic phoenix, so I'm scaling down the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joint positions to bring the wing back to a more balanced size.

I'm also working out the wing's raised pose angle and lift, and planning to layer in leading-edge coverts and crimson-gold feather detailing along the arm with rows of smaller covert cards near the feather bases.

Still generating covert geometry...

For coverts I'll rig them rigidly to the arm joints (elbow/wrist/shoulder) rather than giving them independent joints. For the tail, I'm planning a short 2-3 joint base chain running from the pelvis backward, with a fan of feathers—around nine streamers—radiating from the tail base.

Each streamer sweeps outward and back using a curved path defined by a few control points, tapering to a thin ribbon cross-section, and I need to make sure the lowest point of each curve stays slightly above the ground. I'm also working out how to orient the ribbon's width consistently along the curving path using transport framing rather than a fixed horizontal direction.

I'm thinking about adding ornamental details like gold eyespot accents near the streamer tips, using distance from the centerline at a given point along the path to place the spot correctly across the ribbon's width.

I'm also planning flame-colored glow details at the streamer tips, and considering the head crest—working out whether to make the plumes rigid or flexible chains, with three central ones as jointed chains for movement.

Adding long ear/cheek feathers to match the crest, plus eye decals and crimson brow sweeps with a cream face mask. For the jaw I'm setting a hinge joint near the back-bottom of the head to drive the lower beak sweep, skipping a tongue detail for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the beak shape using local head-bone coordinates for forward, up, and side offsets, painting it with a gold-to-dark gradient and adding small nostril dots, then placing the skull sphere's center and scale in that same local frame.

Still shaping the beak geometry... Now for the lower jaw I'm tapering it similarly, positioned so the tip meets under the upper hook with a slight gap for a resting, nearly-closed mouth. Next I need to figure out eye placement as decals on the sides of the skull.

Placing the eyes symmetrically around 55-62° azimuth with a smaller texture size to keep the atlas light, then moving on to the gold ornament details—starting with a thin circlet looped around the forehead, where I'm working out the right way to anchor the loop to the skull surface.

Now I need to figure out the correct orientation for the circlet's cutting plane so it wraps horizontally around the head like a headband rather than vertically from ear to ear; tilting the direction vector slightly so it sits just above the forehead and dips lower at the back seems like the right approach.

I'm also planning a forehead gem with an octahedron glow set in a gold bezel with leaf motifs, then moving on to the neck collar -- a loop around the body's neck sweep using a tangent-facing frame so the band sits perpendicular to the neck tube.

For the collar itself, I'm sweeping a hexagonal gold ring, then adding a pendant and tassel cards hanging from the front, using path-sampled frames oriented upward rather than tangent-facing so the cords dangle naturally despite the neck's lean. Next I'm thinking through the wing bracers -- gold cuffs with filigree scrollwork wrapped around the wing forearm, built either as a closed-loop sweep or lathe-style band.

For the wrist cuff, I'm layering two thin gold rings plus a raised gem stud rather than trying a single box-section band, since the axis orientation for a flat band around the arm is ambiguous. I'm also planning gold anklet and toe-cap accents for the legs, and sketching out a filigree SVG decal -- an ornate sun-like pectoral ornament radiating from a central gem -- to conform over the chest via decal mapping.

Beyond the filigree, I want feather-trimmed tassels at the collar, ankle, and tail, plus flame-card wisps glowing along the wing trailing edges, tail base, and crest for that ember-bright plumage look. I'm keeping the flat color palette tight, under 64 distinct strings, to stay within budget.

Before I draft the cards, I need to check how `b.cards` and `glow` actually work together — whether glow accepts the mesh array cards returns directly — so I'm going to look at glow.ts and frame.ts for the exact types and exports before writing anything.

input.command: cat kits/glow.ts | head -60; ls samples scratch 2>/dev/null | head; grep -n "export" src/builder.ts | head -60
